Bhagavad Gītā 8.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.12: Having restrained all the gates of the body (sense-organs), having confined the mind in the heart, having placed the prāṇa in the head, established in yogic concentration (yoga-dhāraṇā) —

Bhagavad Gītā 8.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.13: Uttering Om — the single-syllable Brahman — and remembering Me, whoever departs leaving the body — that person attains the supreme destination (paramāṃ gatim).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.14: O Pārtha, for one who continuously and constantly remembers Me with an undivided mind (ananya-cetāḥ) — for that ever-united yogī, I am easily attained (sulabhaḥ).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.15: Having attained Me, those great souls (mahātmānaḥ) who have reached the highest perfection do not take birth again in this transient abode of suffering (duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.16: O Arjuna, all the worlds — up to and including the realm of Brahmā (Brahmaloka) — are subject to return (punar āvartinaḥ). But O Kaunteya, having reached Me, rebirth does not occur.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.17: Those who know that the day of Brahmā extends to a thousand yugas, and that the night of Brahmā also extends to a thousand yugas — they know the reality of day and night.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.18: At the coming of Brahmā's day, all manifest beings arise from the Unmanifest (avyakta); at the coming of night, they dissolve into that same Unmanifest.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.19: O Pārtha, this same multitude of beings (bhūta-grāmaḥ), arising again and again, dissolves helplessly (avaśaḥ) at the coming of night and rises again at the coming of day.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.20: But beyond that Unmanifest, there is yet another eternal Unmanifest — which does not perish even when all beings perish.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.21: That which is called the Unmanifest, the Imperishable (akṣara) — that they call the supreme destination (paramāṃ gatim). That which, having attained, none return — that is My supreme abode (tad dhāma paramaṃ mama).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.22: O Pārtha, that Supreme Puruṣa is attained through undivided devotion (ananyā bhakti) — in whom all beings abide, and by whom all this is pervaded.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.23: O best of the Bharatas, I will describe the times (paths) in which yogīs departing attain non-return (anāvṛttim — liberation) and return (āvṛttim — rebirth).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.24: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight (śukla-pakṣa), and the six months of the northern solstice (uttarāyaṇa) — departing in these, the knowers of Brahman (brahma-vidaḥ) go to Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.25: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa-pakṣa), and the six months of the southern solstice (dakṣiṇāyana) — in these, the yogī reaches the lunar light (cāndramasaṃ jyotir) and returns.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.26: These two paths — the bright (śukla) and the dark (kṛṣṇa) — are considered eternal (śāśvate) for the world. By one, non-return (liberation) is attained; by the other, one returns again.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.27: O Pārtha, knowing these two paths, no yogī is deluded. Therefore, O Arjuna, be yoga-yukta (united with yoga) at all times.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.28: Whatever meritorious fruits have been declared for the study of the Vedas, for sacrifices, for austerities, and for charitable gifts — the yogī who knows all this transcends all of these and attains the supreme, primordial abode (paraṃ sthānam ādyam).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.1: The Blessed Lord said: To you who are free from envy, I shall now fully declare this most secret knowledge combined with direct realization, knowing which you shall be liberated from all that is inauspicious.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.2: This is the sovereign knowledge, the sovereign secret, the supreme purifier; directly perceptible, in accordance with dharma, very easy to practice, and imperishable.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.3: O scorcher of foes, those persons who have no faith in this dharma, not attaining Me, return to the path of death and rebirth.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.4: By Me, in My unmanifest form, this entire universe is pervaded. All beings exist in Me, yet I am not contained within them.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.5: Nor do beings rest in Me — behold My divine mystery (yoga)! My Self, which brings forth and sustains all beings, does not dwell within them.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.6: Just as the mighty wind, moving everywhere, eternally abides in space (ākāśa), so understand that all beings abide in Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.7: O son of Kunti, all beings merge into My nature at the end of a kalpa (cosmic cycle), and at the beginning of the next kalpa, I send them forth again.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.8: Presiding over My own nature, I project forth again and again this entire multitude of beings, which are helpless, being subject to the force of nature (prakṛti).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.9: And these actions do not bind Me, O Dhanañjaya, for I remain seated as one indifferent (udāsīnavat), unattached to those actions.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.10: Under My superintendence, O Kaunteya, Nature (prakṛti) brings forth the moving and the unmoving. By this reason the world revolves (is constantly in flux).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.11: Fools disregard Me when I dwell in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.12: Those of bewildered mind take refuge in the deluding nature of demons and fiends — their hopes are vain, their actions vain, their knowledge vain.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.13: But O Pārtha, great souls (mahātmās), sheltered in the divine nature, worship Me with undivided mind, knowing Me as the imperishable origin of all beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.14: Always singing My glories, striving with firm resolve, bowing before Me with devotion — these ever-steadfast ones worship Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.15: And others, worshipping through the sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña), worship Me as the One, as the Distinct, and in many forms facing all directions.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.16: I am the ritual (kratu), I am the sacrifice (yajña), I am the oblation to ancestors (svadhā), I am the medicinal herb (auṣadha), I am the sacred mantra, I am the clarified butter (ājya), I am the sacred fire, and I am the act of offering.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.17: I am the father of this universe, the mother, the sustainer, the grandsire; I am the knowable (vedyam), the purifier, the syllable Oṃ; and I am the Ṛg, the Sāma, and the Yajur Veda.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.18: I am the goal, the sustainer, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, the selfless friend; I am origin and dissolution, the foundation, the resting place, and the imperishable seed.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.19: I give heat; I withhold and I send forth the rain; I am immortality and also death; I am both being (sat) and non-being (asat), O Arjuna.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.20: The knowers of the three Vedas, who drink the soma and are purified of sin, worship Me through sacrifices, praying for passage to heaven. They reach the holy realm of Indra and enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods in heaven.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.21: Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, when their merit is exhausted, they re-enter the mortal world. Thus, following the dharma of the three Vedas, those who desire enjoyment attain only the cycle of coming and going.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.22: For those persons who worship Me with undivided devotion, meditating on My transcendental form — to those ever-steadfast ones I personally carry what they lack and preserve what they have (yoga-kṣemam).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.23: O Kaunteya, even those devotees who, endowed with faith, worship other gods — they too worship Me alone, but in an improper (unregulated) manner.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.24: For I am the only enjoyer and the only Lord of all sacrifices. Those who do not know Me in truth fall down (from their attainment).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.25: Worshippers of the gods go to the gods; those devoted to ancestors reach the ancestors; those who worship spirits go to the spirits; and those who worship Me come to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.26: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water — that offering of love from the pure-hearted one I accept.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.27: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give in charity, whatever austerity you practice — O Kaunteya, do that as an offering to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.28: Thus you shall be liberated from the bondage of actions with their good and evil results. With the spirit disciplined in the yoga of renunciation (sannyāsa-yoga), you shall become free and come to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.29: I am equal toward all beings; none is hateful to Me and none is dear. Yet those who worship Me with devotion are in Me, and I am also in them.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.30: Even if a person of very evil conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, he must be regarded as righteous (sādhu), for he has resolved rightly.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.31: He swiftly becomes a righteous soul and attains everlasting peace. O Kaunteya, declare with certainty: My devotee is never lost.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.32: O Pārtha, even those who may be born of sinful wombs — women, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras — even they, taking refuge in Me, attain the supreme destination.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.33: How much more, then, the pure Brāhmaṇas and the devoted royal sages! Having obtained this transient and joyless world, worship Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.34: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, bow down to Me. Having thus disciplined yourself, with Me as your supreme goal, you shall come to Me alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.1: The Blessed Lord said: O mighty-armed, hear once more My supreme word, which I shall speak to you with love, desiring your welfare.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.2: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know My origin, for I am in every way the ultimate source (ādi) of the gods and great sages.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.3: He who knows Me as unborn (aja), without beginning (anādi), and the great Lord of all worlds — among mortals, he is undeluded, and is freed from all sins.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.4: Intelligence, knowledge, freedom from delusion, patience, truth, self-restraint of the senses, calmness of mind, pleasure, pain, birth, death, fear, and fearlessness —

Bhagavad Gītā 10.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.5: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and infamy — these diverse states of beings all arise from Me alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.6: The seven great sages of old, and the four (Sanaka and his brothers) before them, and the Manus — born from My mind, imbued with My power — from them come all the creatures of the world.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.7: He who knows, in truth, this My divine glory (vibhūti) and power (yoga) — he becomes united with Me through unwavering yoga. Of this there is no doubt.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.8: I am the source of all; everything proceeds from Me. Knowing this, the wise, endowed with true feeling, worship Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.9: With their minds fixed on Me, with their life-breath offered to Me, enlightening each other, and always speaking of Me, they are ever contented and delighted.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.10: To those who are ever devoted, who worship Me with love — I give that yoga of intelligence (buddhi-yoga) by which they come to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.11: Out of compassion for them alone, dwelling within their very being, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the brilliant lamp of knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.12: Arjuna said: You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode (dhāma), the supreme purifier. You are the eternal, divine Puruṣa, the primordial God (ādideva), unborn and all-pervading (vibhu).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.13: All the sages declare this of You — the divine sage Nārada, Asita, Devala, and Vyāsa — and You Yourself tell me so.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.14: All this that You tell me, O Keśava, I hold to be true. O Lord (Bhagavan), neither the gods nor the demons know Your true manifestation.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.15: You alone know Yourself by Yourself, O Puruṣottama, O source of beings (Bhūtabhāvana), O Lord of beings (Bhūteśa), O God of gods (Devadeva), O Lord of the universe (Jagatpate).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.16: You alone are worthy of fully declaring Your own divine glories (vibhūtis) — by which manifestations You pervade and stand in these worlds.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.17: O Yogin, O Lord, how may I know You, always meditating? And in which particular forms (bhāvas) are You to be contemplated by me?

Bhagavad Gītā 10.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.18: Tell me again in full, O Janārdana, of Your yoga-power and divine glories — for in listening to this nectar (amṛtam), I am never satisfied.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.19: The Blessed Lord said: Very well! I shall tell you of My divine glories, O best of the Kurus — but only the principal ones, for there is no end to My extent.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.20: O Guḍākeśa (conqueror of sleep), I am the Self (ātman) dwelling in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.21: Among the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; among lights, the radiant sun; among the Maruts I am Marīci; among the stars I am the moon.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.22: Among the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; among the gods I am Vāsava (Indra); among the senses I am the mind; and among beings I am consciousness (cetanā).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.23: Among the Rudras I am Śaṅkara (Śiva); among the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas I am Kubera (Vitteśa, lord of wealth); among the Vasus I am Pāvaka (fire); and among mountains I am Meru.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.24: O Pārtha, know Me as Bṛhaspati, the chief among priests; among generals I am Skanda; among bodies of water I am the ocean.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.25: Among the great sages I am Bhṛgu; among words I am the single syllable Oṃ; among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition (japa-yajña); and among immovable things I am the Himālaya.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.26: Among all trees I am the aśvattha (peepal/sacred fig); among the divine sages I am Nārada; among the Gandharvas I am Citraratha; among the Siddhas I am the sage Kapila.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.27: Among horses know Me as Uccaiḥśravas, born of the nectar-churning; among the lordly elephants, Airāvata; and among men, the king.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.28: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt (vajra); among cows, the wish-fulfilling cow (Kāmadhuk); among progenitors I am Kandarpa (Kāmadeva, god of love); among serpents I am Vāsuki.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.29: Among the Nāgas I am Ananta (Śeṣa); among aquatic beings I am Varuṇa; among the ancestors I am Aryamā; among those who maintain order I am Yama.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.30: Among the Daityas I am Prahlāda; among reckoners I am Time (Kāla); among beasts I am the lion (king of animals); and among birds I am Vainateyā (Garuḍa).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.31: Among purifiers I am the wind (Pavana); among weapon-bearers I am Rāma; among fish I am the Makara (crocodile/sea-monster); and among rivers I am the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.32: O Arjuna, I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all creations. Among all knowledge-systems I am the science of the Self (adhyātma-vidyā); and among those who reason and debate, I am the truth-seeking argument (vāda).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.33: Among letters I am the letter 'A'; among grammatical compounds I am the dvandva (copulative compound). I am imperishable Time itself, and I am the Creator facing in all directions (viśvatomukha).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.34: I am death that seizes all, and I am the origin of those yet to be born. Among the feminine virtues, I am Fame (Kīrti), Prosperity (Śrī), Speech (Vāk), Memory (Smṛti), Intelligence (Medhā), Steadfastness (Dhṛti), and Forbearance (Kṣamā).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.35: Among the Sāma hymns I am the Bṛhatsāma; among poetic meters I am the Gāyatrī; among months I am Mārgaśīrṣa (November–December); and among seasons I am the flower-bearing spring (Kusumākara).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.36: Among the deceitful I am gambling (dyūta); I am the splendor of the splendorous; I am victory; I am resolute effort (vyavasāya); and I am the goodness (sattva) of the good.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.37: Among the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva (Krishna Himself); among the Pāṇḍavas I am Dhanañjaya (Arjuna); among sages I am Vyāsa; and among poets I am Uśanā (Śukrācārya).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.38: Among those who punish and subdue, I am the Rod of Chastisement (Daṇḍa); among those who seek to win, I am statecraft (Nīti); among secrets I am Silence (Mauna); and I am the knowledge of those who know.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.39: And whatever is the seed-cause of all beings, O Arjuna, that too am I. There is no being — moving or unmoving — that can exist without Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.40: O Parantapa, there is no end to My divine manifestations. What I have declared is only an indicative enumeration (uddeśataḥ) — a sample — of My infinite glory.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.41: Whatever being is endowed with glory (vibhūtimat), or is prosperous (śrīmat), or is powerfully vigorous (ūrjitam) — know that every such being arises from but a spark of My splendor.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.42: Or rather, O Arjuna, what is the use of this much detailed knowledge for you? I pervade and sustain this entire universe with but a single fraction (ekāṃśena) of Myself — and yet remain.
